summary: Fail. The code of tasks 4.13q and 4.13r matches its contract and every gate passes at HEAD: quota.test.ts 30/30, credential-provider.test.ts 22/22, review-run.test.ts 65/65, all exit 0, and no fake-opencode or quota-server process of this audit stayed behind. The guard matches a real NUL-split argv, resolves paths before the boundary compare, checks the recorded starttime before KILL, and the two runners hold byte-identical guard functions. The live export selects by integrationID with named no-entry and ambiguous refusals, which addresses the 04:35 seed refusals. quota.ts keeps its one-line JSON output, exit 0 on every state, exit 2 on a bad flag. One blocking gap stays in the wiring: no production path reads the Go quota through ra-quota. quota.ts runs ra-quota only when BENCH_RA_QUOTA is set, no production file sets it, and both drivers export BENCH_QUOTA_BASE and curl the OpenChamber endpoint directly, so the 5 s direct read that timed out at 04:35 and refused route 3 is unchanged in every real run. The 01:45 probe of 2026-11-20 is therefore not guaranteed a result on the two opencode-go routes, and the seed fix stays unproven against the live store until that probe runs.
blocking_findings: F1: The PM order 'read the Go quota through ra-quota' is not wired into any production path. harness/model-guide/quota.ts:408-420 reads ra-quota only when BENCH_RA_QUOTA is set; the plan row 4.13r names '/home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-pr/scripts/jobs/ra-quota' as the production default, but quota.ts holds no default branch, so with the seam unset the opencode-go read falls through to the direct GET with a 5 s bound. Nothing in production sets the seam: a repository-wide grep finds BENCH_RA_QUOTA only in quota.ts, quota.test.ts, and the plan and run logs, and no systemd user unit sets it. The production drivers keep the direct path: /home/daniebo/.local/share/lending-desk-bench/model-guide/jobs/probe-4.10.sh:15,20,54 exports BENCH_QUOTA_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:38307 and curls http://127.0.0.1:38307/api/quota/opencode-go directly with a 20 s bound; night-4.11.sh:15,30,69 does the same. The 04:35 probe proved the failure mode: measure/runs/model_guide/probe-4.10.txt:4 holds 'opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash refused review-run: the probe refused: the quota state is stopped: quota: the quota read timed out exit=2'. The ra-quota source with its 60 s bound, 120 s cache, and last-good fallback, the entire point 8 fix, never engages in a real run, so the phase goal of first track A results by 2026-11-22 stays exposed to the same refusal. Route to Green: give quota.ts the production default of the plan row for the opencode-go provider, or have both drivers export BENCH_RA_QUOTA=/home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-pr/scripts/jobs/ra-quota and read their own skip check through ra-quota; the driver edit sits outside this repository, so the orchestrator applies it.
nonblocking_findings: N1: The plan row 4.13r (measure/tracks/model_guide/plan.md:2396 area) claims 'Nothing in this repo sets BENCH_QUOTA_BASE outside tests'. The production drivers of this track set it on every real run (probe-4.10.sh:15, night-4.11.sh:15). The false claim hid the production gap of F1; correct the row when F1 closes.

N2: The drivers enforce only the upper bound of the PM real-call window. probe-4.10.sh:100 stops after 05:55 and night-4.11.sh:126 stops after 05:00, but no lower bound exists, so a probe started at 01:45 +07 makes real calls before the approved 02:00 start (plan.md:1816, 1864). The PM must approve the earlier start, or the probe must wait until 02:00, or the drivers need a lower bound.
evidence: Contract 1, the ra-quota source: quota.ts:342-373 runs '${BENCH_RA_QUOTA} status --json' with a 90 s bound, parses .["opencode-go"].windows percents, and falls back to the RA_QUOTA_LASTGOOD file with a 6 h staleness rule; quota.ts:407-420 gates all of it on BENCH_RA_QUOTA and holds no production default. The real ra-quota matches the parse: 'ra-quota status --json' prints {plan: {state, windows: {name: {percent, reset_ms}}}} and its lastgood file holds {plans: {plan: {fetchedAt, windows}}} (advantage-pr/scripts/jobs/ra-quota:1672-1680, 1335-1345, 598-632), the same shapes quota.ts reads. Output line and exit codes are unchanged: quota.ts:126-141 emits one JSON line on stdout, one 'quota: <reason>' stderr line on stopped, exit 0 on every state, exit 2 on a bad flag.

Contract 2, the live export selection: provider-credential.sh:150-155 selects entry.integrationID === provider with entry.active === true; the SELECT_JS fail lines are 'the store holds no active entry of provider

' (154) and 'the store holds two active entries of provider

: ambiguous' (155); the shell maps them to 'the store holds two active entries of provider

: ambiguous' (240 seed, 260 scan-values) and, for a non-ambiguous seed failure, to 'the credential seed failed' (242), which the runner reports as 'the provider credential seed failed' (review-run.sh:710); scan-values alone also refuses 'the store holds no entry of provider

' (262). The live store entry holds integrationID, active, and value with type/access/refresh and no provider field (measure/tracks/opencode_executor/evidence/auth-export.shape.json), so the 04:35 seed refusals of probe-4.10.txt:2-3 came from the old provider-field selection and the integrationID selection of 4.13r addresses them, conditional on the shared store holding exactly one active entry per integrationID (opencode-go for routes 1 and 3, opencode for route 2); this audit cannot read the live store, because the role rules forbid every opencode call.

Contract 3, the guard lines: 'the job root must be an absolute path' and 'the job root could not be resolved' and 'the job HOME is outside the job root' (review-run.sh:697-704, judge-run.sh:477-483, provider-credential.sh:57-61); 'the call HOME must be an absolute path' and 'the call HOME is outside the job root' (provider-credential.sh:70-76); the INFRA lines are 'review-run: INFRA stopped daemon <pid>' (review-run.sh:501) and 'judge-run: INFRA stopped daemon <pid>' (judge-run.sh:396).

Contract 3, the guard behavior: daemon_pids joins the NUL-separated cmdline before the 'serve --service' match and resolves home, cwd, and the job root with realpath before the boundary compare in both runners (review-run.sh:405-451, judge-run.sh:300-346); stop_daemons records field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat at TERM and skips the KILL on a starttime mismatch (review-run.sh:462-489, judge-run.sh:367-394). The functions daemon_pid_alive, daemon_starttime, and daemon_pids are byte-identical between the two runners, and stop_daemons differs only in the INFRA line prefix, verified by sed extraction of each function from both files.

Contract 4, the drivers: /home/daniebo/.local/share/lending-desk-bench/model-guide/jobs/probe-4.10.sh:14-15,20,52-79 and night-4.11.sh:14-15,30,65-94 read the Go quota by 'curl -s --max-time 20 http://127.0.0.1:38307/api/quota/opencode-go' and export BENCH_QUOTA_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:38307; neither sets BENCH_RA_QUOTA. They do need the ra-quota source: the PM order names ra-quota, and the direct path already refused one route at 04:35. The 20 s driver curl succeeded at 04:35 and the runner's 5 s read of the same endpoint timed out, so both levels gain from the 60 s bound, the 120 s cache, and the last-good fallback of ra-quota.

Contract 5, the 04:35 probe at HEAD c46161f (measure/runs/model_guide/probe-4.10.txt:1-6): route 1 'opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash refused review-run: the provider credential seed failed exit=2'; route 2 'opencode/hy4-flash-free refused review-run: the provider credential seed failed exit=2'; route 3 'opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash refused review-run: the probe refused: the quota state is stopped: quota: the quota read timed out exit=2'; 'left processes: 0'.

Contract 5, the 01:45 probe answer: not guaranteed. Route 2 (opencode/hy4-flash-free) needs no quota read and is cleared in code by the integrationID seed fix, so its remaining conditions are the live store holding one active opencode entry and the PM approving the 01:45 start. Routes 1 and 3 (opencode-go) carry the same two conditions plus the unmitigated quota path of F1: the driver-level curl answers within 20 s or the route is skipped with 'Go quota read failed', and the runner-level 5 s direct read can refuse again exactly as at 04:35, because the ra-quota fallback never engages in production. A Go quota over the night limits (5h >= 95 or weekly >= 100) also skips both Go routes by design, and tonight's night runs then skip every route too, because night-4.11.sh:61-62 greps '^<route> reachable' in probe-4.10.txt, which currently holds only refusal lines.

Gates at HEAD 1572612, one file at a time, fakes only: 'cd harness && npx vitest run model-guide-tests/quota.test.ts --configLoader native --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot' gives 'Tests 30 passed (30)' exit 0; 'cd harness && npx vitest run model-guide-tests/credential-provider.test.ts --configLoader native --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot' gives 'Tests 22 passed (22)' exit 0; 'bun test harness/model-guide-tests/review-run.test.ts' gives '65 pass, 0 fail' exit 0. After each run the pgrep scans for fake-opencod[e] and quota-serve[r] showed nothing of this audit; the one transient quota-server seen right after the bun run belonged to a concurrent 'bun test harness/model-guide-tests/review-run.test.ts' of another session (pid 1822402, started 06:15:04) and exited with that run; no process of this audit's temp folders stayed behind.
